writes.rule: Per subtopic seen: pMastery 0.7 if right at D2/D3, 0.55 if right at D1, 0.25 if wrong; level L0-L3 from the ladder step reached
Prerequisite-gap index = 100 x weighted misses / weighted items seen in slots 1-4, averaged over groups
Groups with the highest Part A percent (top 1-2, only if >= 65%)
Groups with the lowest Part A percent (bottom 1-2, only if < 65%)
Calibration = 1 - mean |confidence/5 - correct| over Part A (feeds the first MCI reading)
Highest difficulty answered correctly twice in a row: D1 low, D2 medium, D3 high
Verbal reasoning = percent of Part B verbal items right
Numerical reasoning = percent of Part B numerical items right
Abstract reasoning = percent of Part B abstract items right
Spatial reasoning = percent of Part B spatial items right
Logical deduction = percent right on Part B items tagged p65
Numeracy fluency = numerical percent scaled by speed (right answers under target time count 1.2x, max 100)
Processing speed = 100 x share of Part B items answered right within target seconds
RIASEC profile: each career-interest item scored 1-5; letter score = mean of its 2 items; top 3 letters form the code (e.g. IRC)

items.markingKey: C. 6. The largest number dividing both

items.stem: Why does the smell of perfume spread across a still room?
items.answer: Its particles diffuse, moving randomly from high to low concentration
options: Air pushes the perfume in one direction
Its particles diffuse, moving randomly from high to low concentration
Perfume is lighter than air, so it only rises
items.markingKey: C. Its particles diffuse, moving randomly from high to low concentration. Random particle motion spreads the perfume out

items.stem: Which of these is a compound?
items.markingKey: A. water. Water is hydrogen and oxygen chemically joined; air is a mixture

items.stem: Which statement about a mixture of iron filings and sulfur powder is true?
items.answer: The iron can be separated with a magnet
options: The iron can be separated with a magnet
items.markingKey: C. The iron can be separated with a magnet. In a mixture each substance keeps its own properties

items.stem: Pressure is
items.subtopicHint: Pressure as force per unit area
items.markingKey: B. force per unit area. p = F / A

items.stem: Why is it easier to cut with a sharp knife than a blunt one?
items.answer: The sharp edge has a smaller area, so the same force gives more pressure
items.subtopicHint: Pressure as force per unit area
options: Blunt knives only have more friction
Sharp knives push with more force by themselves
The sharp edge has a smaller area, so the same force gives more pressure
items.markingKey: D. The sharp edge has a smaller area, so the same force gives more pressure. Smaller area, larger pressure

items.stem: A box weighing 600 N rests on a base of area 0.5 m². What pressure does it exert on the floor?
items.subtopicHint: Pressure as force per unit area

items.stem: Which part of a cell controls its activities?
items.subtopicHint: Cell structure: plant and animal cells
items.markingKey: D. nucleus. The nucleus holds the genetic instructions

items.stem: Onion peel cells and cheek cells are viewed under a microscope. Which difference will you see?
items.answer: Onion cells have a cell wall and a regular shape; cheek cells do not
items.subtopicHint: Cell structure: plant and animal cells
options: Cheek cells have a large central vacuole
Onion cells have a cell wall and a regular shape; cheek cells do not
items.markingKey: D. Onion cells have a cell wall and a regular shape; cheek cells do not. Only plant cells have cell walls

items.stem: A cell placed in pure water swells but does not burst. Which cell is it most likely to be?
items.answer: A plant cell, because its cell wall resists bursting
items.subtopicHint: Cell structure: plant and animal cells
options: A plant cell, because its cell wall resists bursting
Any cell, since water never enters cells
An animal cell, because it has a cell membrane
items.markingKey: A. A plant cell, because its cell wall resists bursting. Animal cells without a wall can burst in pure water

items.stem: A cyclist covers 150 m in 30 s. What is her average speed?
items.markingKey: A. 5 m/s. v = s / t

items.stem: On a distance-time graph, a horizontal line shows that the object is
items.markingKey: D. stationary. Distance is not changing

items.stem: A car's distance-time graph is a straight line from (0 s, 0 m) to (20 s, 300 m). What is its speed?
items.markingKey: C. 15 m/s. Gradient = 300 ÷ 20

items.stem: Acceleration is
items.markingKey: D. change in velocity ÷ time taken. a = Δv / t

items.stem: A car speeds up from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 4 s. What is its acceleration?
A speed-time graph rises steadily from 0 to 12 m/s in 6 s. How far does the object travel in that time?
items.markingKey: B. 36 m. Area of the triangle = ½ x 6 x 12

items.stem: The proton number of an atom is the number of
items.subtopicHint: Chemistry: proton number, mass number and isotopes
items.markingKey: B. protons in its nucleus. Also called the atomic number

items.stem: An atom of sodium has proton number 11 and mass number 23. How many neutrons does it have?
items.subtopicHint: Chemistry: proton number, mass number and isotopes

items.stem: Chlorine-35 and chlorine-37 are
items.answer: isotopes: atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
items.subtopicHint: Chemistry: proton number, mass number and isotopes
options: isotopes: atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
items.markingKey: B. isotopes: atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. Same element, different mass number

items.stem: Which structure is found in plant cells and bacterial cells but not in animal cells?
items.subtopicHint: Biology: animal, plant and bacterial cells
items.markingKey: A. cell wall. Bacteria have walls but no nucleus

items.stem: Bacterial cells differ from plant and animal cells because their DNA is
items.subtopicHint: Biology: animal, plant and bacterial cells
items.markingKey: A. not enclosed in a nucleus. Bacteria have a circular chromosome in the cytoplasm

items.stem: A cell has a cell wall, many chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole. Where is it most likely from?
items.answer: the palisade layer of a leaf
items.subtopicHint: Biology: animal, plant and bacterial cells
options: the palisade layer of a leaf
items.markingKey: D. the palisade layer of a leaf. Root hair cells have no chloroplasts

items.stem: The ground is wet and people are carrying umbrellas. It ___ have rained.
items.markingKey: C. must. 'Must have' expresses a confident deduction

items.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly as direct speech?
items.markingKey: B. "Close the window," said Mother.. Only the spoken words go inside the quotation marks, followed by a comma

items.stem: Change to indirect speech: She said, 'I will call you tomorrow.'
items.answer: She said that she would call me the next day.
options: She said she will called me tomorrow.
She said that she would call me the next day.
She told that she would calls me the next day.
She said that I will call you tomorrow.
items.markingKey: B. She said that she would call me the next day.. 'Will' becomes 'would', 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'

items.stem: Which is the best title for a paragraph about saving water by fixing leaks, using buckets and reusing water?
items.markingKey: A. Simple Ways to Save Water. A title should cover the main idea of the whole paragraph

items.stem: Read: "Mangroves grow along tropical coasts. Their tangled roots hold soil in place, slow down storm waves and shelter young fish. Many mangrove forests are being cleared for farms and buildings." Which summary is best?
items.answer: Mangroves protect coasts and wildlife but are being cleared
options: Farms are more important than mangroves
Mangroves protect coasts and wildlife but are being cleared
items.markingKey: D. Mangroves protect coasts and wildlife but are being cleared. A summary keeps the main points and leaves out detail

items.stem: Which sentence would NOT belong in a summary of a text explaining how vaccines work?
items.answer: My cousin was scared of injections when he was little.
options: My cousin was scared of injections when he was little.
Vaccines train the immune system to recognise germs.
This prepares the body to fight infection quickly.
items.markingKey: A. My cousin was scared of injections when he was little.. Personal anecdotes are not main points

items.stem: 'Silent sea, softly sighing' mainly uses
items.markingKey: C. alliteration. The repeated 's' sound

items.stem: 'I have told you a million times!' is an example of
items.markingKey: D. hyperbole. Deliberate exaggeration for effect

items.stem: What is the effect of the simile in 'Her words were as sharp as broken glass'?
items.answer: It shows her words were hurtful
options: It shows her words were hurtful
items.markingKey: D. It shows her words were hurtful. Broken glass cuts, so the words wounded

items.stem: A text with headings, numbered steps and diagrams explaining how to set up a new phone is most likely
items.markingKey: D. an instruction manual. Its purpose is to instruct

items.stem: A blog post uses informal language, jokes and the word 'you' a lot. What are its likely audience and purpose?
items.answer: Teenagers, to entertain and engage them
options: Teenagers, to entertain and engage them
The government, to announce a law
Lawyers, to set out a contract
items.markingKey: A. Teenagers, to entertain and engage them. Tone and register suggest the reader

items.stem: A charity letter begins: 'Imagine walking six miles every day just to fetch water.' Why does it begin this way?
items.answer: To make the reader empathise and feel involved before asking for help
options: To instruct the reader how to walk
To make the reader empathise and feel involved before asking for help
items.markingKey: C. To make the reader empathise and feel involved before asking for help. Second-person imagining draws the reader in

items.stem: 'The arid land had not seen rain for months.' 'Arid' means
items.subtopicHint: Meaning of unfamiliar vocabulary from context
items.markingKey: B. very dry. 'Not seen rain' is the clue

items.stem: 'Despite the ominous clouds, the picnic went ahead.' 'Ominous' suggests the clouds
items.subtopicHint: Meaning of unfamiliar vocabulary from context
items.markingKey: A. threatened bad weather. 'Despite' signals a reason not to go ahead

items.stem: 'His explanation was so convoluted that nobody could follow it.' 'Convoluted' means
items.subtopicHint: Meaning of unfamiliar vocabulary from context
items.markingKey: B. complicated and hard to follow. 'Nobody could follow it' is the clue

items.stem: 'Mira slammed her books on the desk and refused to look at anyone.' How is Mira most likely feeling?
items.subtopicHint: Implicit meaning: inferring thoughts and feelings
items.markingKey: B. angry or upset. Actions reveal feelings

items.stem: 'The house was spotless; every cushion stood to attention.' What does this suggest about the owner?
items.answer: They are very tidy, perhaps strict about order
items.subtopicHint: Implicit meaning: inferring thoughts and feelings
options: They are very tidy, perhaps strict about order
items.markingKey: B. They are very tidy, perhaps strict about order. 'Stood to attention' suggests military neatness

items.stem: 'Grandfather's chair stayed by the window, though no one sat in it any more.' What is implied?
items.answer: Grandfather has died or gone away, and the family keeps the chair in his memory
items.subtopicHint: Implicit meaning: inferring thoughts and feelings
options: Grandfather has died or gone away, and the family keeps the chair in his memory
items.markingKey: B. Grandfather has died or gone away, and the family keeps the chair in his memory. 'No one sat in it any more' hints at absence

items.stem: Which word has the most positive connotation?
items.markingKey: C. slim. The others suggest unhealthiness

items.stem: A writer describes a crowd as 'a swarm'. What does this suggest?
items.answer: The crowd is large, fast-moving and perhaps threatening, like insects
options: The crowd is large, fast-moving and perhaps threatening, like insects
items.markingKey: C. The crowd is large, fast-moving and perhaps threatening, like insects. Swarm brings insect associations

items.stem: Compare 'The old man shuffled' with 'The old man walked'. What does 'shuffled' add?
items.answer: It suggests he is frail or tired, moving slowly without lifting his feet
options: Nothing; the two mean the same
It shows he is in a hurry
It suggests he is frail or tired, moving slowly without lifting his feet
items.markingKey: C. It suggests he is frail or tired, moving slowly without lifting his feet. Precise verbs carry connotation

items.stem: Which was a long-term cause of the First World War?
items.answer: The alliance system that divided Europe into two armed camps
items.subtopicHint: Causes of the First World War
options: The alliance system that divided Europe into two armed camps
items.markingKey: B. The alliance system that divided Europe into two armed camps. The other three came after 1918

items.answer: European powers were weakened by war and nationalist movements had grown stronger

European powers were weakened by war and nationalist movements had grown stronger
The League of Nations ordered it
items.markingKey: B. European powers were weakened by war and nationalist movements had grown stronger. Both a weaker centre and stronger demands

items.stem: On a climate graph, rainfall is usually shown as
items.subtopicHint: Reading climate graphs and climate zones
items.markingKey: B. bars. Temperature is the line; rainfall is the bars

items.stem: A place is hot all year and gets over 2000 mm of rain a year. Its climate is most likely

items.markingKey: C. tropical rainforest. Hot and wet all year

items.answer: Hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters
items.subtopicHint: Reading climate graphs and climate zones
options: Hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters
items.markingKey: B. Hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters. Seasonal contrast in rainfall is the key

items.stem: The Triple Entente was made up of
items.markingKey: C. Britain, France and Russia. Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy formed the Triple Alliance

items.stem: Where was Archduke Franz Ferdinand assassinated in June 1914?
items.markingKey: B. Sarajevo. Sarajevo, in Bosnia

items.stem: Explain why a local crisis in the Balkans in 1914 became a wider war.
items.answer: The alliance system drew the great powers in one after another
options: The alliance system drew the great powers in one after another
items.markingKey: C. The alliance system drew the great powers in one after another. Austria-Hungary, Russia, Germany, France and Britain were bound by alliances; the League did not yet exist

items.stem: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in
items.subtopicHint: History: terms of the Treaty of Versailles
items.markingKey: B. 1919. Signed on 28 June 1919

items.stem: Which was a term of the Treaty of Versailles?
items.answer: Germany's army was limited to 100 000 men
items.subtopicHint: History: terms of the Treaty of Versailles
options: Germany joined the League of Nations at once
Germany's army was limited to 100 000 men
items.markingKey: C. Germany's army was limited to 100 000 men. Alsace-Lorraine went to France; Germany lost its colonies

items.stem: Why did many Germans call the treaty a 'diktat'?
items.answer: It was imposed on Germany without negotiation
items.subtopicHint: History: terms of the Treaty of Versailles
options: It was imposed on Germany without negotiation
items.markingKey: D. It was imposed on Germany without negotiation. Diktat means a dictated peace

items.stem: A six-figure grid reference locates a point to the nearest

items.subtopicHint: Geography: grid references, scale and direction

items.subtopicHint: Geography: grid references, scale and direction
items.markingKey: C. a steep slope. Height changes quickly over a short distance

items.stem: At a conservative plate boundary, the plates
items.markingKey: B. slide past each other. As on the San Andreas Fault

items.stem: Why do volcanoes form at destructive plate boundaries?
items.answer: The denser oceanic plate is subducted and melts, and the magma rises
options: The plates slide past each other
The denser oceanic plate is subducted and melts, and the magma rises
items.markingKey: D. The denser oceanic plate is subducted and melts, and the magma rises. Subduction produces magma

items.stem: Iceland has many volcanoes but few deep earthquakes. Why?
items.answer: It sits on a constructive boundary where magma rises as plates separate
options: It is on a destructive boundary
It is on a conservative boundary
It sits on a constructive boundary where magma rises as plates separate
items.markingKey: D. It sits on a constructive boundary where magma rises as plates separate. Constructive boundaries give shallow quakes and frequent eruptions
